principle: Classification must answer WHAT IS THIS DOCUMENT, not WHAT DOES IT MENTION (mission Section 3). The general, legal-drafting-convention fact this fix leans on: a document's own caption/self-description ALWAYS appears at or near the very top of its own text, and any mention of an OTHER document type it references, requires, or attaches (a table-of-contents/exhibit-list entry, a cross-reference, a required-delivery clause) necessarily appears LATER in the text. Text POSITION is therefore a general, structural, non-package-specific proxy for 'is this evidence about the document itself, or about something the document merely mentions.'
mechanism: Tier 2's fallback scan is changed from 'return the type of the FIRST RULE (by array index) that matches anywhere in the 3000-char preamble' to 'return the type whose EARLIEST textual match position across ALL rules is smallest.' RULES array order becomes irrelevant to Tier 2's outcome except as an ambiguity tiebreaker input (see below) - the array order that previously drove which type won now only matters for readability/maintenance grouping, exactly as the file's own existing header comment already describes its INTENT to be ('more specific patterns checked before their generic parents') without that intent actually working correctly for the compliance-certificate-vs-credit-agreement shape.
explicitlyRejectedApproaches: Reordering RULES to put CREDIT_AGREEMENT/INDENTURE/base types before COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE/GUARANTEE/etc. - this is exactly the 'keyword arms race' the mission prohibits (section 5): it would fix THIS specific ordering collision while leaving the underlying defect (array-order, not evidence-quality, decides the winner) fully intact for the next unseen shape.

A bounded fixed-character title-zone window (e.g. first N characters) - rejected because a real SEC filing's confidentiality-redaction banner/exhibit-cover-page length varies unpredictably before the actual caption begins, and a fixed window either misses genuine captions that start late or fails to exclude a TOC/exhibit entry that happens to fall within the same window on a differently-formatted document.

Reusing document-identity.ts's own single title-line regex/extraction directly as the classifier's primary signal - considered, but rejected as the SOLE mechanism because it requires a specific line-start/suffix-word shape (AGREEMENT/INDENTURE/CERTIFICATE/LETTER/JOINDER) that not every real classification RULE type's own title convention satisfies (e.g. a bare 'GUARANTY' title, already handled by an existing Tier-2 pattern) - the position-based approach below generalizes to every existing RULE without requiring a second, narrower title-matching grammar to be kept in sync with the first.

A hand-maintained list of 'low-quality mention' keywords (Exhibit/Schedule/Annex/Form of) to suppress - rejected as its own kind of keyword arms race; the position-based mechanism achieves the same practical effect (TOC/exhibit entries lose) without needing to enumerate every possible low-quality-context marker phrase.
algorithmSummary: 1. For every RULE in the existing RULES array (order unchanged, still used only for the tiebreaker in step 4), find the EARLIEST match position across ALL of that rule's own alternative patterns in the 3000-char preamble (a generalization of the existing findEvidence, which only returned the first PATTERN-array-order match, not the earliest TEXT-position match among a rule's own alternatives).

2. Across all rules with at least one match, select the rule whose earliest match position is numerically smallest (ties broken by original RULES array order, preserving the existing composite/specific-before-generic intent for the vanishingly rare case of two rules matching literally the same character index).

3. AMBIGUITY GUARD: check whether any OTHER rule (of a genuinely DIFFERENT, non-overlapping type) has a match whose text SPAN does not overlap the winning match's own span, AND both matches fall within a bounded early 'caption zone' (first 500 chars) AND within a bounded gap of each other (150 chars) - i.e. two genuinely disjoint, comparably-early, comparably-prominent signals with no clear single winner. If found, return safe uncertainty (doc.declaredType ?? UNKNOWN, low confidence, resolutionMethod DETERMINISTIC_CAPTION_AMBIGUOUS) rather than an arbitrary confident pick.

4. The OVERLAP check in step 3 is what keeps this safe for existing composite/specific types: AMENDED_AND_RESTATED_AGREEMENT's own pattern textually CONTAINS a nested 'credit agreement'/'indenture'/'loan agreement' substring (so its own match span always overlaps the corresponding base-type match span) - these are correctly recognized as the SAME evidence, not two competing candidates, so no false ambiguity is ever raised for an amended-and-restated agreement, a supplemental indenture, or a composite guarantee-and-security agreement.

5. If exactly one rule wins with no disjoint early conflict, return it with the SAME shape/confidence/resolutionMethod values Tier 2 already used (DETERMINISTIC_TITLE_PATTERN / DETERMINISTIC_DECLARED_TYPE_CONFIRMED) - this is a behavior-PRESERVING change for every case where the earliest-evidence rule and the array-order-first rule already happen to coincide (true for essentially every existing passing test, since real captions are almost always both the earliest AND, incidentally, near the front of the array's own intended specific-to-generic grouping).
Tier 1 (self-referential '(this "X")' title) is left completely unchanged and still runs first, unaffected by any of the above.
newResolutionMethod: DETERMINISTIC_CAPTION_AMBIGUOUS (added to the DocumentClassification.resolutionMethod union) - the only new literal value introduced.
noKeywordArmsRaceConfirmation: The RULES array itself, its patterns, and their relative order are NOT modified at all. No Riot, Coinbase, or known-package string is added anywhere. No section-number exception is added. The fix changes HOW the array is searched (earliest-position selection instead of array-order selection), never WHAT it searches for.

expectedGenericTestOutcomes.C1_TOCContainsComplianceCertificateForm: CREDIT_AGREEMENT - the document's own earlier caption wins over the later TOC/exhibit entry.
expectedGenericTestOutcomes.C2_FullComplianceCertificateFormAttached: CREDIT_AGREEMENT - the attached form's own 'Compliance Certificate' text is necessarily later than the base agreement's own caption.
expectedGenericTestOutcomes.C3_ActualComplianceCertificateReferencin: COMPLIANCE_CERTIFICATE - its own caption is earliest; later body references to 'the Credit Agreement' come after.
expectedGenericTestOutcomes.C4_AmendmentContainingOriginalTitle: AMENDMENT (or the appropriate existing amendment type) - the amendment's own caption/numbering is textually earliest; the referenced original agreement's title appears later in the same recital.
expectedGenericTestOutcomes.C7_IntercreditorReferencingSeveralCredit: INTERCREDITOR_AGREEMENT - its own caption is earliest; the several referenced credit agreements are necessarily later, and (being MULTIPLE, same-type) do not create a false ambiguity signal on their own since they compete with each other, not with the winning INTERCREDITOR_AGREEMENT match, and the ambiguity guard only compares the WINNING match against other types.
expectedGenericTestOutcomes.C8_ConflictingHighQualityTitleEvidence: Safe uncertainty (declaredType/UNKNOWN, DETERMINISTIC_CAPTION_AMBIGUOUS) - two disjoint, comparably-early, different-type captions with no established composite RULES entry for their combination.
expectedGenericTestOutcomes.C9_MisleadingTOCTitleBeforeActualBodyTit: Actual primary document identity wins IF the real caption's own match position is still earlier than the misleading TOC entry's position (this is the realistic case for every real SEC-filed financing document this codebase has ever encountered - the caption always precedes the TOC). A pathological fixture where a TOC genuinely precedes the real caption is a materially different real-world shape from anything evidenced in this codebase's own fixtures (FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR/Riot) and is treated in the generic test as a fixture explicitly checked to confirm this - if it does not hold, this is disclosed as a residual limitation, not silently claimed fixed.
expectedGenericTestOutcomes.C10_MultipleExhibitFormNamesInsideBaseAg: Base agreement classification remains stable - every exhibit/form name necessarily appears after the base agreement's own caption.
